statements.t: “Based on this performance and our confidence in the outlook for the rest of the year, we are once again raising the midpoints of our financial guidance ranges across all key metrics.

Also, consistent with our disciplined and balanced capital allocation strategy, we continued returning additional value to shareholders in the quarter and expect the Pacira transaction to have minimal impact on our gross leverage ratio upon expected closing by the end of November.”

• The Company generated approximately $115 million in new product revenues (approximately $287 million for the year) and now expects to deliver approximately $450 million in new product revenues in full-year 2026.
The Company expects to resume production at the facility during the first quarter of 2027.

The Company estimates the total revenue impact of supply constraints was approximately $100 million in the third quarter of 2026 and currently anticipates an impact of approximately $100 million to total revenues in the fourth quarter of 2026.
The Company is not providing forward-looking guidance for U.S.
With respect to the guidance ranges as provided on August 6, 2026, at that time the Company did not provide forward-looking guidance for U.S.

However, the Company has not quantified future amounts to develop this target but has stated its goal to manage notional gross debt and Adjusted EBITDA over time in order to generally maintain or reach the target.

• the possibility that the Company may be unable to achieve intended or expected benefits in connection with divestitures, acquisitions, strategic alliances, collaborations, or other transactions, or restructuring programs, within the expected timeframes or at all;

• the possibility that the Company may not complete the proposed acquisition of Pacira within the timeframe it anticipates or at all and, if completed, the possibility that the Company may not realize the anticipated benefits, synergies and operating efficiencies of the proposed acquisition;

• any changes in or difficulties with the Company’s manufacturing facilities, including with respect to short- or long-term shutdowns, inspections, remediation and restructuring activities, supply chain continuity, inventory management, or the ability to meet anticipated demand;
• the Company’s failure to achieve expected or targeted future financial and operating performance and results;

• the effect of any changes in the Company’s or its partners’ customer and supplier relationships and customer purchasing patterns, including customer loss and business disruption being greater than expected following an adverse regulatory action, acquisition or divestiture;
We expect that any reduction in that funding will have a negative impact on our financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.
Certain markets in which we do business outside of the U.S. have undergone government-imposed price reductions, and further government-imposed price reductions are expected in the future.
The Company expects to fund the transaction primarily from excess cash with the remainder from short-term borrowings.

These restructuring activities are expected to optimize the Company’s commercial capabilities, enabling functions, R&D, medical affairs and regulatory activities, and sourcing, manufacturing and supply chain activities, including inventory optimization.
As a result, the Company expects a global workforce reduction of up to approximately 10%.
The Company anticipates that these restructuring activities, as well as associated costs and savings, will be completed primarily over the three years ending 2028.
The Company expects to record charges for costs associated with the restructuring activities of the EWSR.
For the committed restructuring activities, the Company expects to incur total pre-tax charges ranging between $700 million and $850 million.

In addition, management believes the potential savings related to these committed restructuring activities will be between $600 million and $700 million once fully implemented, with most of these savings expected to improve operating cash flow.

While product continues to be shipped from the Indore facility to markets outside the U.S., as expected, we have also experienced a negative impact in other markets, including the ARV business in Emerging Markets and select generic products in Europe.
We have been in regular communication with the FDA during this process and will continue working to satisfy the FDA that the steps we have taken have resolved all the points raised.
The timing of the reinspection will be determined by the FDA; however, we anticipate that the facility will be ready for reinspection in 2026.
The Company expects to resume production at the facility during the first quarter of 2027.

The foregoing manufacturing suspension is expected to result in incremental costs associated with the Company’s remediation activities, operational inefficiencies, reduced production volumes and delays in production during the affected period.
The Company currently anticipates the negative impact of these supply disruptions to be approximately $100 million to total revenues in the fourth quarter of 2026.
Also, due to timing of the expected ramp up needed to get the facility back to full production in 2027, the Company currently does not expect to recover the lower revenues from 2026 in 2027.
We will continue to work closely with our customers to mitigate the effects of potential supply disruptions to meet the needs of the patients we serve.
Actual internal and forecasted operating results and annual budgets used by management include adjusted net earnings and adjusted EPS.

We believe that net cash provided by operating activities and available liquidity will continue to allow us to meet our needs for working capital, capital expenditures, interest and principal payments on debt obligations, dividend payments, and share repurchases.

Nevertheless, our ability to satisfy our working capital requirements and debt service obligations, and fund planned capital expenditures, share repurchases, or dividend payments, will substantially depend upon our future operating performance (which will be affected by prevailing economic conditions), and financial, business and other factors, some of which are beyond our control.

The Company anticipates having sufficient liquidity, including existing borrowing capacity under the 2024 Revolving Facility, Commercial Paper Program, and Receivables Facility combined with cash to be generated from operations, to fund foreseeable cash needs without requiring the repatriation of non-U.S. cash.
In addition, we plan to continue to explore various other ways to unlock the value of the Company’s unique global platform in order to create shareholder value.
The Company is in compliance with its covenants at September 30, 2026 and expects to remain in compliance for the next twelve months.

While the Company believes that it has meritorious defenses with respect to the claims asserted against it and the assumed legal matters referenced above, and intends to vigorously defend its position, the process of resolving these matters is inherently uncertain and may develop over a long period of time, and so it is not possible to predict the ultimate resolution of any such matter.
